the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Choose V' around the generic orbit points as in the invariant-affine-open lemma; since U without V is closed, j is an immersion and V(I) union j(U) is closed, there is an ideal J inside I with V(J) = V(I) union j(U without V), for instance the ideal of elements of I vanishing on j(U without V); replacing the groupoid, j and I by their restrictions to V' with J, one may assume U is affine and s, t finite locally free. Pick f in I not vanishing at any point of the R-orbits of u_1, ..., u_m (algebra silly lemma) and form the norm g = Norm_s of t^sharp composed with j^sharp(f). Since f in I and V(I) union j(U) is closed, U intersect D(f) to D(f) is a closed immersion, hence f^n g is the image of an element h in I for some n > 0. By the determinant trick lemma g is R-invariant, so D(g) is R-invariant; f does not vanish on the orbit of u_j, so g does not vanish at u_j; and V(g) contains V(j^sharp(f)), whence j^{-1}D(h) = D(g), an R-invariant affine open containing the orbit points. (source lines 2935-2962)
